largest_vegas_favorite.note: Largest Vegas favorite this week (-550 ML, ~85% raw implied) — by policy we don't crown a pick on raw favorite status alone. It went through the same Advocate/Skeptic/Arbiter debate as everyone else (see its entry below) and still ranks #1 post-debate, but the recommendation goes to the next-best team instead.

process_note: Each shortlisted team's case was built by an Advocate (live research), stress-tested by an independent Skeptic subagent looking only for flaws, and resolved by an independent Arbiter subagent that weighed both sides without seeing the raw research trail. Teams outside the top-10 shortlist got a lighter single-pass positives/negatives note instead of the full three-stage debate.

board.summary: The Advocate's case is essentially structural — Arizona benched its franchise QB for a game-manager backup, which is close to a fatal roster decision for Week 1. The Skeptic's injury notes are real but describe players still expected to suit up; the line movement (11.5 → 9.5-10.5 despite lopsided public money) is the one point with teeth, trimming the edge slightly without erasing it.
positives: -550 ML (~85% raw implied) at home in a dome
Arizona benched franchise QB Kyler Murray for backup Jacoby Brissett
negatives: Justin Herbert nursing a plantar fasciitis issue from camp (mobility/timing risk)
EDGE Tuipulotu (hip) and LT Slater (recovering from patellar tendon tear, 'flare-up' in pads) both banged up
Spread has fallen 11.5 → 9.5-10.5 despite ~79% of money on LAC — sharp money/books less convinced than the raw line suggests
Arizona retains real skill talent (Marvin Harrison Jr., James Conner); Brissett is low-ceiling but not turnover-prone
trap_flags: reverse line movement — spread fell from 11.5 to 9.5-10.5 despite ~79% of public money on LAC, suggesting sharp/book skepticism
board.head_to_head: Chargers lead 11-5 all-time; Arizona is 1-7 on the road in this series (lone road win in 2001), though ARI won the most recent meeting 17-15 in Oct. 2024.
board.venue_history: First-ever Chargers-Cardinals meeting at SoFi Stadium (opened 2020) — no venue-specific trend yet; Arizona's broader 1-7 road record vs. LAC is the closest context.
board.rest_prep: Week 1 for both teams — no bye or short week for anyone; no rest/prep edge either way.

board.summary: The Skeptic's strongest thread (Verse addition, unknown new DC) mostly restates general Week 1 uncertainty rather than specifically favoring Cleveland, and 'trap game' chatter is narrative, not evidence. The core fact — a declining Deshaun Watson leading a rebuilding team with a new HC/DC on the road — still dominates, so the Advocate's number holds with only a minor discount.

Cleveland in a full rebuild under new HC Todd Monken, having just traded away Myles Garrett
Deshaun Watson fully healthy but in visible decline
negatives: Cleveland got a quality DL piece (Jared Verse) back in the Garrett trade; new DC Mike Rutenberg is a total unknown
JAX's own HC publicly said he has 'no idea' what Cleveland will run defensively
Local coverage openly debating this as a trap game after a surprise 13-4 season raised expectations
Actual line (-8.5) is a field goal shy of what an 82% ML would typically imply — market hedging more than the raw number suggests
trap_flags: post-breakout trap-game narrative (surprise 13-4 season raising expectations)
new-system uncertainty (Cleveland has a brand-new, unproven DC)

board.summary: The Skeptic lands a real blow here: two starting safeties on PUP and the starting CB released is a specific, verifiable, high-impact weakness — not vague pessimism — and it's exactly the kind of hole a hot-closing Saints passing attack could exploit. Combined with a 49.5 total signaling a competitive script, the safe-floor case is meaningfully weaker than the raw -334 ML suggests.
positives: -334 ML / -6.5 at home
Jared Goff healthy, one of the league's better offenses
negatives: Both starting safeties (Kerby Joseph, Brian Branch) opened on PUP; starting CB Terrion Arnold was released — secondary genuinely depleted
Lost both coordinators after 2024 (Ben Johnson to CHI, Aaron Glenn to NYJ); replacements only in year two
Saints closed 2025 hot and are veteran/division-tested despite being battered
49.5 total prices in a shootout, not a blowout
board.head_to_head: Series is nearly even at 13-13-1 (Saints also won a 2011 playoff meeting); Lions hold a 7-4 edge at home vs. New Orleans.
board.venue_history: No notable trend — Saints' results at Ford Field have been mixed historically.
board.rest_prep: Week 1 for both teams — no bye or short week for anyone; no rest/prep edge either way.

trap_game_policy_note: Trap-game status is capped at the 1-2 most credible upset risks per week (LAC, JAX this week), not a flag for every minor concern. Any trap-flagged team is automatically excluded from the recommendation, same as the largest Vegas favorite — both LAC (largest favorite) and JAX (trap game) were excluded here, so the recommendation goes to DET, the highest-probability team left standing.
